note.question: What determines transforming offline algorithms to their online counterparts?
note.overview: Motivated by online decision making in time-varying combinatorial environments, we study the problem of transforming offline algorithms to their online counterparts. We focus on offline combinatorial problems that are amenable to a constant factor approximation using a greedy algorithm that is robust to local errors. For such problems, we provide a general framework that efficiently transforms offline robust greedy algorithms to online ones using Blackwell approachability.

source.section: Blackwell Sequential Games and Approachability
source.quote: In the Blackwell sequential game (X,Y,p), a target set S is g(T)-approachable if there exists a player 1 strategy such that for every player 2’s strategy, the resulting sequence of actions satisﬁes d∞ 1 T T X t=1 p(xt,yt),S ! ≤g(T), where for any vector w ∈Rd and set S ⊆Rd, d∞(w,S) ≜infv∈S ∥w −v∥∞is the ℓ∞-distance of vector w from set S.
